title: Liyasa site configuration
description: The definition of `liyasa.json` (PRD §8). This file is the single source of truth: §8's tables are generated from it, the Rust `SiteConfig` is generated from it by typify, and `liyasa schema config` emits it verbatim. Any key referenced anywhere in the PRD must exist here.

$schema.description: URL of this schema; carries the `v1` major version.

name.description: Site name. The only required key.

description.description: One-line description of the site, used as the default meta description and as the site summary in the agent surfaces when a page carries none of its own.

root.description: Content root, relative to the config file.

public.description: `false` requires an access mode under `auth` and a server; rejected with E0120 before 0.5.

logo.description: The site logo, per colour scheme. Leave it out and a text logo is generated from `name`.

light.description: Path or URL of the logo shown in the light scheme; also the fallback when `dark` is absent.

dark.description: Path or URL of the logo shown in the dark scheme. Absent, the light logo is used in both.

favicon.description: The site favicon, per colour scheme. Absent, one is generated from the logo.

light.description: Path or URL of the favicon a browser in the light scheme asks for; also the fallback when `dark` is absent.

dark.description: Path or URL of the favicon a browser in the dark scheme asks for, for the browsers that ask for one.

preset.description: Layout preset: a complete set of tokens and partial overrides the rest of `theme` adjusts. Changing it changes the whole look, not one value.

colors.description: The colour roles the token set is built from. Every value is any CSS colour; what is not set keeps the preset's.

primary.description: The accent a reader acts on: buttons, links, focus rings. Adapted per scheme unless `light` and `dark` set their own, and reported with E0107 when no label colour on it clears WCAG AA.

light.description: The primary to use in the light scheme, as written, instead of adapting `primary` to it.

dark.description: The primary to use in the dark scheme, as written, instead of adapting `primary` to it.

text.description: Body text on the page background, and the label the contrast check considers for a fill.

muted.description: Secondary text: captions, metadata, the parts of the chrome that should recede.

border.description: Rules and outlines: table borders, card edges, the line under a heading.

accent.description: A second accent for highlights that should not read as the primary action.

success.description: The status colour for a successful or affirmative callout.

warning.description: The status colour for a cautionary callout.

danger.description: The status colour for a destructive or error callout.

background.description: The page background per colour scheme, which every derived surface and tint is mixed against.

light.description: Page background in the light scheme.

dark.description: Page background in the dark scheme.

codeTheme.description: Syntax highlighting, one theme per colour scheme, emitted as CSS variables so switching schemes needs no re-render.

light.description: Bundled Shiki theme for the light scheme, or `css-variables` to drive the colours yourself.

dark.description: Bundled Shiki theme for the dark scheme, or `css-variables` to drive the colours yourself.

fonts.description: The three type faces the site ships. A face named here is self-hosted at build time, so no third-party font request happens at runtime.

heading.description: The face headings are set in.

family.description: CSS font family name, and the Google Fonts family to fetch when `source` says so.

weight.description: Weight or weight range to ship, as a CSS value such as `600` or `600 700`. Shipping fewer weights ships fewer bytes.

source.description: A Google Fonts family, downloaded and self-hosted at build time, or a local file path.

format.description: Font file format, such as `woff2`, when it cannot be inferred from the source.

body.description: The face body text is set in.

family.description: CSS font family name, and the Google Fonts family to fetch when `source` says so.

weight.description: Weight or weight range to ship, as a CSS value such as `400` or `400 700`. Shipping fewer weights ships fewer bytes.

source.description: A Google Fonts family, downloaded and self-hosted at build time, or a local file path.

format.description: Font file format, such as `woff2`, when it cannot be inferred from the source.

mono.description: The face code blocks and inline code are set in.

family.description: CSS font family name, and the Google Fonts family to fetch when `source` says so.

weight.description: Weight or weight range to ship, as a CSS value such as `400`. Shipping fewer weights ships fewer bytes.

source.description: A Google Fonts family, downloaded and self-hosted at build time, or a local file path.

format.description: Font file format, such as `woff2`, when it cannot be inferred from the source.

subset.description: Accepted and ignored with W0716 until the fontations subsetter exists.

icons.description: Where an icon name resolves from. An icon may also be written as an emoji, a URL, a path to an SVG, or inline SVG, and only the icons a build uses are bundled.

library.description: The icon set a bare icon name is looked up in. Lucide, Phosphor, and Tabler ship as they are; Font Awesome Free ships with the attribution its licence requires.

defaultType.description: The Font Awesome style a name with no style prefix takes, such as `solid` or `regular`.

appearance.description: Which colour scheme a reader arrives in, and whether they may change it.

default.description: The scheme a first-time reader sees. `system` follows the operating system and is applied before first paint, so there is no flash.

background.description: Decoration behind the page background, for a site whose landing pages want one.

image.description: Path or URL of an image drawn behind the page.

color.description: A flat colour drawn behind the page, under any image.

decoration.description: A generated pattern drawn behind the page: a grid, a gradient, or window chrome. `none` leaves the background flat.

layout.description: The page's proportions and its two visual dials, density and roundness.

sidebarWidth.description: Width of the navigation sidebar, as a CSS length.

contentWidth.description: Maximum width of the prose column, as a CSS length. Wider fits more code; narrower reads better.

tocWidth.description: Width of the on-page table of contents, as a CSS length.

density.description: How much air the chrome gets. `compact` tightens spacing and type scale for a dense reference site.

radius.description: Corner radius for cards, buttons, and inputs, as a CSS length. `0` squares everything off.

shadows.description: Whether elevated surfaces cast a shadow. Off, they are separated by borders alone.

oneOf.description: One stylesheet, relative to the project root.
Several stylesheets, loaded in the order given.

css.description: Custom stylesheet or stylesheets, loaded after the theme's own so they win on equal specificity.

oneOf.description: One script, relative to the project root.
Several scripts, loaded in the order given.

js.description: Custom script or scripts, deferred after the theme runtime.

theme.description: Presets, colours, fonts, icons, appearance, layout, and overrides (§8.2).

href.description: Where the link goes; absolute for an external destination, a route for one inside the site.

icon.description: Icon shown before the label, resolved the way `theme.icons` says.

primary.description: The call to action at the end of the navbar: one button, or the repository link.

type.description: `button` renders `label` and `href` as written; `github` renders the repository link with its star count, fetched at build time and cached, never from the reader's browser.

label.description: The button's text. Unused by the `github` form, which labels itself.

href.description: Where the button goes. For the `github` form, the repository URL whose stars are counted.

oneOf.description: The navigation tree itself, as an array of nodes.
Path to a navigation file (CFG-34).
The navigation tree with its settings: the tree under `pages` or `tabs`, and the three switches that apply to all of it.

breadcrumbs.description: What sits above a page title: the full trail (`path`), the section name alone (`eyebrow`), or nothing.

autofill.description: During `dev`, append pages that are in the project and not in this tree to an "Other" group, so a new page is visible the moment it is written. A `build` warns with W0130 instead of appending.

drilldown.description: Navigate to a group's first page when the group is expanded, rather than only opening it.

pages.description: The navigation tree, when the site has no tabs.

tabs.description: The navigation tree, when the top level is tabs; each tab carries its own sidebar.

navigation.description: The navigation tree, a file that holds it, or an object carrying tree options (§8.4).

socials.description: Social links, keyed by platform (`x`, `github`, `linkedin`, `discord`, `slack`, `youtube`, `bluesky`, `mastodon`, `website`, or your own name with an icon). Each renders as an icon with an accessible label.

links.description: Link columns, in the order they are written.

footer.description: Footer socials, link columns, branding, and legal line (§8.5).

placeholder.description: Placeholder text in the search field. Localizable.

shortcut.description: Keyboard shortcut that opens search, written as a chord such as `mod+k`, where `mod` is Command on macOS and Control elsewhere.

boost.description: Rules that move results up or down the ranking.

match.description: A path glob or a group name the rule applies to.

factor.description: How much to multiply the score by. Above 1 promotes, below 1 buries.

exclude.description: Globs kept out of the index entirely. An excluded page is still routable; it is simply not findable.

maxResults.description: How many results one query returns.

snippets.description: Whether a result carries a matching excerpt. Off, results are titles alone and the index is smaller.

filters.description: The facets a reader may filter results by.

shardSize.description: Target size range for one index shard. Smaller shards mean more requests and less downloaded per query; larger ones the reverse.

mode.description: `keyword` searches the index alone. `hybrid` also uses the assistant's embeddings, which needs a server.

search.description: Search behaviour and the browser index's shard sizing (§8.6).

metatags.description: Meta tags added to every page, keyed by name. A page's own front matter overrides one of them.

organization.description: A schema.org Organization, emitted as JSON-LD on every page. Pages also emit TechArticle and BreadcrumbList without being asked.

indexing.description: `navigable` makes only pages reachable from the navigation indexable; `all` indexes every page the build produces.

trailingSlash.description: Whether a route ends in a slash. The server redirects the other form with a 301, so only one of the two is canonical.

robots.description: Extra rules appended to the generated `robots.txt`.

oneOf.description: `false` writes no sitemap at all.
Sitemap settings, including a sitemap per locale.

sitemap.description: Whether a sitemap is written, and how.

crawlers.description: Per-bot directives, keyed by user agent (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `Google-Extended`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Bytespider`, and the rest). They become user-agent groups in `robots.txt` and a section of `llms.txt`. The default allows everyone: agents reading the docs is the point.

allow.description: Let this crawler read the site.

disallow.description: Keep this crawler out of the site.

paths.description: Limit this crawler to these paths, rather than allowing or refusing the whole site.

canonicalOrigin.description: Production origin used for absolute URLs in `llms.txt`, feeds, and the Markdown directive.

seo.description: Meta tags, JSON-LD, indexing, sitemap, robots, and crawler directives (§8.7).

content.description: The banner's text, as Markdown. It is rendered at build time, so a banner costs the reader no script.

dismissible.description: Whether a reader may close the banner. A dismissal is remembered against `id`.

id.description: What a dismissal is remembered against. Change it to show a closed banner again; absent, the content is its own identity.

by_locale.description: Per-locale text, keyed by locale code, used instead of `content` for a reader in that locale.

start.description: When the banner begins showing, as `YYYY-MM-DD` or an RFC 3339 timestamp. Compared against the build clock, not the reader's, so an unstarted banner is simply absent from the output.

end.description: When the banner stops showing, as `YYYY-MM-DD` or an RFC 3339 timestamp. An expired banner is absent from the output rather than hidden by a script.

404.description: The page a reader gets when nothing is at the address they asked for. It always answers with HTTP 404, whatever it renders.

redirect.description: Send the reader to the home page instead of showing a 404 page. Off by default, because a redirect hides the broken link that caused it.

description.description: Body of the 404 page, as Markdown.

page.description: A page of your own to render instead, by path.

placement.description: Where the actions sit: above the page, in the sidebar, or both.

items.description: The actions offered on every page, in the order they appear.

oneOf.description: A built-in action by name, such as `copy-markdown`, `view-markdown`, `copy-mcp-url`, `download-pdf`, or one of the `open-in-*` handoffs to an assistant.
An action of your own.

href.description: Where the action goes. The page's own URL can be interpolated into it.

exclude.description: Built-in actions to drop, so the rest of the default list can stay untouched.

thumbnails.description: How the Open Graph card is drawn for a page that has no image of its own. The card is generated from the page's title and description and is deterministic: the same page and configuration produce the same bytes.

appearance.description: `dark` draws the card from the dark scheme's tokens; anything else uses the light scheme's.

background.description: Card background, as any CSS colour. Absent, the theme's page background is used.

font.description: CSS font stack the card's text is set in.

logo.description: A logo placed in the card's corner, as a path or a data URI.

oneOf.description: On or off, using the default engine.
The engine to render with.

math.description: Whether `$...$` and `$$...$$` are rendered as mathematics, and by which engine.

html.description: What happens to raw HTML in a page: `allow` keeps it, `sanitize` keeps what the allow list permits, `off` drops it and reports it.

wikilinks.description: Whether `[[Page]]` links resolve against the content tree. Off by default, because the brackets mean nothing in CommonMark.

related.description: Related-page links at the foot of a page.

auto.description: Choose related pages automatically when a page names none of its own.

frontmatter.description: How strictly front matter is read.

strict.description: Unknown front matter keys become warnings.

templating.description: The template layer that runs before Markdown is parsed.

undefined.description: What a template does with a name nothing defines: `strict` fails the build, `lenient` renders a visible marker in its place.

limits.description: Caps that stop one page's template from running away with the build.

iterations.description: How many loop iterations one page may run.

depth.description: How deep includes and blocks may nest.

codeblocks.description: Defaults for every fenced code block; a block's own info string still wins.

lineNumbers.description: Number the lines of a code block.

wrap.description: Wrap long lines instead of scrolling them sideways.

theme.description: Override `theme.codeTheme` for code blocks in content.

images.description: How a content image is turned into the set of files a reader is served.

breakpoints.description: Widths, in pixels, that each image is resized to for the `srcset`.

formats.description: Formats each image is encoded in, most preferred first; a browser takes the first it understands.

customElements.description: What happens to an unknown HTML element: `strip` removes it and keeps its children, `keep` passes it through.

lastModified.description: CFG-74: show the git or editor timestamp on every page.

oneOf.description: A version by name alone. Written this way, the first in the list is the default.
A version with its own routing and labelling.

name.description: The version's name, which is what a navigation subtree binds to and what appears in the URL.

default.description: The version served at the unprefixed route. Exactly one version carries it, or E0108 is reported.

label.description: What the version switcher shows instead of the name.

path.description: A route prefix of your own, instead of the version's name.

tag.description: Badge for this version in the switcher: `latest`, `deprecated`, `beta` (CM-93).

oneOf.description: A locale by code alone. Written this way, the first in the list is the default.
A locale with its own labelling.

code.description: BCP 47 code, such as `en` or `pt-BR`, which is what a navigation subtree binds to and what appears in the URL.

default.description: The locale served at the unprefixed route. Exactly one locale carries it, or E0108 is reported.

label.description: What the locale switcher shows, in that locale's own language.

locales.description: Languages this site is published in (§7.11).

name.description: The dimension's name, which is what a page reads and what a navigation subtree binds to.

values.description: The values this dimension may take. A page that reads the dimension is built once per value.

default.description: The value a reader who has chosen none is served.

label.description: What the switcher calls this dimension.

dimensions.description: Custom content dimensions such as product (§7.12).

name.description: The variation's name, as a page refers to it.

label.description: What a reader sees this variation called.

variations.description: Named content variations a page may belong to.

oneOf.description: The rules alone, as shorthand for an object with `rules`.

source.description: The route to redirect from. A segment written as `:name` is a parameter and may be used in the destination.

destination.description: Where the reader is sent. An absolute URL needs its host in `externalAllow`, and a parameter may not appear in a host.

status.description: The HTTP status the redirect answers with: 301 for a permanent move, 302 for a temporary one.

oneOf.description: The redirect rules and the hosts an absolute destination may name.

rules.description: The redirects, in order. Two rules with the same source are reported as E0106.

source.description: The route to redirect from. A segment written as `:name` is a parameter and may be used in the destination.

destination.description: Where the reader is sent. An absolute URL needs its host in `externalAllow`, and a parameter may not appear in a host.

status.description: The HTTP status the redirect answers with: 301 for a permanent move, 302 for a temporary one.

externalAllow.description: Hosts an absolute destination may point at. A redirect to any other host is refused with E0109, so a config edit cannot quietly send readers off the site.

items.description: Hosts an absolute redirect destination may point at (E0109).

redirects.description: Redirect rules, and the hosts an absolute destination may point at (E0109).

oneOf.description: The document's path or URL, when the defaults suit it. Its id is derived from the file name.
The document with settings of its own.

id.description: How navigation and pages refer to this document.

source.description: Path or URL of the document. A remote URL is a trust-plane value: an untrusted build may only use the URLs the deploy branch already names.

overlays.description: Overlay documents applied to the spec in order, which is how a published API is adjusted for the docs without editing the spec itself.

baseUrl.description: Server the playground sends requests to, instead of the one the document names.

oneOf.description: Every operation in the document.
Only these operations, written as `GET /users` or as operation ids.

openapi.description: OpenAPI specifications bound to this site (§13).

oneOf.description: The document's path or URL, when the defaults suit it.
The document with settings of its own.

id.description: How navigation and pages refer to this document.

source.description: Path or URL of the document. A remote URL is a trust-plane value: an untrusted build may only use the URLs the deploy branch already names.

asyncapi.description: AsyncAPI specifications bound to this site.

oneOf.description: The schema's path or URL, when the defaults suit it.
The schema with settings of its own.

id.description: How navigation and pages refer to this schema.

source.description: Path or URL of the schema.

graphql.description: GraphQL schemas bound to this site.

enabled.description: Whether verification runs at all for this site.

policy.description: What each kind of finding costs, keyed by kind (`code`, `facts`, `links`, `screenshots`) and valued by severity. A kind set to `error` fails the build when `build.strictVerification` is on.

sources.description: Truth sources by id, plus the `commands` allow list (VER-25, a trust-plane key per CFG-95).

commands.description: The commands a fact may run to produce a value. A trust-plane key: an untrusted build reads it from the deploy branch, never from the branch being built.

allow.description: The command allow list. A fact that runs anything else is refused rather than executed.

runners.description: The runners checks execute in, keyed by name.

facts.description: Accepted by the schema and read by nothing. RFC 1302 records that neither VER-76 nor the schema says what it should contain.

sandbox.description: Accepted by the schema and read by nothing; `runners.sandbox` is the key that carries the sandbox (RFC 1302).

budget.description: Wall-clock budgets; W0622 queues the remainder when the deploy budget is spent.

schedule.description: When verification runs on its own, as a cron expression, for the checks that are too slow to run on every build.

report.description: Accepted by the schema and read by nothing. RFC 1302 records that neither VER-76 nor the schema says what it should contain.

prose.description: Accepted by the schema and read by nothing. RFC 1302 records that neither VER-76 nor the schema says what it should contain.

screenshots.description: Screenshot comparison settings, including how much a screenshot may differ before it is a finding.

drift.description: How a drift between the docs and their source is reported.

batchSize.description: How many pages one drift pass examines.

autoResolve.description: Close a drift finding automatically once the page and its source agree again.

http.description: How a documented HTTP call is verified: against a mock, against a staging deployment, or both.

target.description: Base URL HTTP checks run against.

external.description: Check links that leave the site. Off, only internal links are checked, which needs no network.

list.description: The regions this site has content for.

default.description: The region a reader is served when none can be determined.

detection.description: How a reader's region is decided, in order: from their identity, from a request header, or from a choice they made.

header.description: The request header a region is read from, such as `CF-IPCountry`. It is only trusted from a peer in `server.trustedProxies`.

availability.description: A facts file saying which features exist in which region, so a page can say so without hard-coding it.

cookieConsent.description: Consent provider, or `true` for Liyasa's built-in banner (CFG-81).

oneOf.description: The provider by name, or `builtin` for Liyasa's own banner.
The provider with its own settings.

provider.description: Which consent provider manages the banner.

oneOf.description: `true` uses the built-in banner; `false` asks for no consent, which only suits a site whose integrations need none.

telemetry.description: Liyasa's own anonymous CLI telemetry; off by default in OSS.

integrations.description: Third-party scripts and consent (§26.8). A vendor key is enabled when present and not `false` or `null`; Liyasa maintains its CSP sources (ANA-62).

llms.description: The `llms.txt` index an agent reads to find its way around the site.

custom.description: A file of your own to publish as `llms.txt` instead of the generated index.

full.description: Also publish `llms-full.txt`, the whole site as one document, for an agent that would rather read everything than navigate.

split.description: Split `llms-full.txt` into several files when one would be larger than the size limit.

markdown.description: The Markdown twin of each page, which is what an agent is served when it asks for the page as text.

includeOpenApiSchema.description: Include the schema of an endpoint's request and response in the Markdown twin of its page.

instructions.description: A line of guidance prepended to every Markdown twin, for whatever an agent should know before reading the site.

skill.description: The agent skill this site publishes about itself.

files.description: The files that make up the skill.

mcp.description: The MCP server this site publishes, so an agent can search and read it through a tool rather than by crawling.

name.description: The server's name as an agent sees it.

description.description: What the server says it is for, which is how an agent decides to use it.

external.description: Other MCP servers to advertise alongside this one. A trust-plane key: an untrusted build reads it from the deploy branch, never from the branch being built.

specVersion.description: The agent-readiness specification version this site targets (SPEC-03).

agents.description: Agent surfaces: llms.txt, Markdown output, skills, MCP (§24, §25).

preview.description: Limits on the preview the editor builds while someone is typing.

maxIterations.description: How many template iterations a preview render may run before it is cut short.

enabled.description: Whether the web editor is available for this site.

branch.description: The branch the editor commits to.

output.description: Directory the built site is written to, relative to the project root.

drafts.description: Include pages marked `draft: true`. Off, they are built by `dev` and left out of `build`.

minify.description: Minify the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript the build emits.

prefetch.description: Prefetch a page when a reader's pointer rests on a link to it.

hashing.description: How an asset's URL carries its content hash: in the file name, as a query parameter, or not at all. `none` makes a build's file names stable at the cost of cacheability.

downloads.description: Whether a downloadable file opens in the browser or is saved, per extension.

pdf.description: `inline` opens a PDF in the browser; `attachment` downloads it.

zip.description: `inline` opens an archive in the browser; `attachment` downloads it.

basePath.description: URL prefix the site is served under, such as `/docs`. It prefixes the links and assets in the output; it does not change where the files are written.

env.description: The environment variables a template may read. Nothing outside this list is visible to `env()`, and each value is part of the build's fingerprint, so changing one rebuilds the pages that read it.

items.description: Environment variables `env()` may read; their values are fingerprinted as build inputs.

budget.description: How long a build may take before it is reported as over budget.

maxVariantsPerPage.description: How many variants one page may expand into before the build refuses. A variant is one combination of the dimensions that page actually reads, so a page that reads none has exactly one.

maxVariants.description: How many variants the whole build may produce before it refuses.

variantDiscoveryIterations.description: How many passes the build makes over a page to discover what it reads. A page whose variables depend on other variables needs more than one.

strictLinks.description: Whether a link to a page or file that does not exist fails the build. Off, it is a warning and the link is left as written.

strictVerification.description: Whether a failed verification check fails the build.

eager.description: Generate every image derivative during the build rather than on first request. Slower builds, no first-request cost.

build.description: Build outputs, budgets, caps, and determinism inputs (§6.6).

mode.description: How a reader proves who they are. `public` asks nothing of them; the rest need `liyasa serve`.

argon2.description: How the password hash is computed. Higher costs are slower to verify and slower to attack; the defaults are the ones to keep unless a measurement says otherwise.

memoryKiB.description: Memory one hash computation uses, in KiB.

iterations.description: How many passes over that memory one hash makes.

parallelism.description: How many lanes a hash computation runs in.

jwt.description: Accepting a token your own system issued.

algs.description: Signature algorithms a token may use. Anything else is refused, which is what stops an `alg: none` token.

iss.description: The issuer a token must claim.

aud.description: The audience a token must claim, so a token minted for another service is not accepted here.

jwksUrl.description: Where the signing keys are published.

loginUrl.description: Where a reader without a token is sent to get one.

groupsClaim.description: The claim a reader's access groups are read from, which is what page and navigation `groups` are matched against.

regionClaim.description: The claim a reader's region is read from.

localeClaim.description: The claim a reader's locale is read from.

oidc.description: Signing in through an OpenID Connect provider.

issuer.description: The provider's issuer URL, from which its endpoints are discovered.

clientId.description: This site's client id at the provider. The client secret lives in the secret store, never here.

scopes.description: Scopes requested at sign-in; ask for the claims the site actually reads and no more.

groupsClaim.description: The claim a reader's access groups are read from.

managed.description: Liyasa's own sign-in, by emailed link.

allowDomains.description: Email domains that may sign in. Empty, nobody can.

session.description: How long a reader stays signed in.

cookieName.description: Name of the session cookie, for a site that shares a domain with something else.

logout.description: What happens after a reader signs out.

redirect.description: Where a reader lands after signing out.

preview.description: Who may see a preview deployment.

protection.description: `org` limits a preview to the organization, `password` to whoever has the password, `public` to anyone with the link.

models.description: Which model answers each kind of request, written as `provider:model`.

providers.description: Per-provider settings. Keys and secrets are never in this file; they live in the secret store.

openai.description: OpenAI, or anything that speaks its API.

baseUrl.description: Where to reach the API, for a proxy or a compatible service.
Where to reach the API, for a proxy or a compatible service.
Where to reach the API, for a proxy or a compatible service.
Where the Ollama instance is listening.

region.description: The AWS region to call Bedrock in.

assistant.description: The assistant a reader can ask questions of.

instructions.description: Standing instructions the assistant follows on this site, such as what to recommend and what to refuse.
Operator text prepended to assistant and agent system prompts.

agent.description: The agent that proposes edits to the documentation itself.

limits.description: How large a change the agent may propose in one go.

maxFilesChanged.description: Most files one proposal may touch.

maxLinesChanged.description: Most lines one proposal may change.

contextRepos.description: Repositories the agent may read for context while it works.

reindex.description: Reindexing the site for the assistant, which costs money each time.

autoApproveCents.description: How much a reindex may cost, in cents, before someone has to approve it.

includePersonalized.description: What the assistant does with content written for one reader: `neutral` answers from the version nobody is personalized into, `exclude` leaves that content out of its index entirely.

respectNoindex.description: Keep pages marked `noindex` out of the assistant's index too, not only out of search engines'.

ai.description: Model routing and assistant, agent, and reindex settings.

collector.description: Static sites: URL of a collector (ANA-09).

db.description: Path or URL of the analytics database (§6.8).

rawSink.description: Where raw events are written before they are aggregated.

rawDays.description: Days of raw events to keep before they are dropped.

aggregateMonths.description: Months of aggregates to keep, which is what the dashboards read.

identityLinkage.description: Link a reader's events to their identity when they are signed in. Off, every event is anonymous.

botList.description: Which list of bot user agents is filtered out of the numbers.

untrustedRunsPerDay.description: How many automation runs a day an untrusted source may cause.

untrustedTokensPerDay.description: How many model tokens a day untrusted runs may spend in total.

untrustedCostCentsPerDay.description: How much untrusted runs may cost a day, in cents.

perSourceHourly.description: How many runs a single source may cause in an hour, so one noisy source cannot use the whole day's budget.

definitions.description: Directory the automation definitions are read from. A trust-plane path: an untrusted build reads it from the deploy branch.

repo.description: The repository to read, as a clone URL or `owner/name`.

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit to read.

paths.description: Only these paths are fetched, which is how a large repository stays affordable to read.

depth.description: How much history to clone. `1` fetches the named ref alone.

trustedProxies.description: CIDRs whose forwarded headers are believed. Until a peer is listed here, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, `CF-Connecting-IP`, and the region headers are ignored, because anyone can send them.

items.description: CIDR. Default none: forwarded-for and region headers are ignored unless the peer is listed.

variantCache.description: The cache of rendered page variants the server keeps in memory.

entries.description: How many variants the cache holds before it evicts the least recently used.

dynamic.description: How pages that cannot be pre-rendered are served on demand.

oneOf.description: One per CPU core.
A fixed number.

concurrency.description: How many on-demand renders run at once.

queue.description: How many renders may wait before further requests are refused rather than queued behind a long line.

rateLimits.description: Requests per minute per client, by what is being asked for. A limit is a ceiling on one client, not on the site.

agentPages.description: Requests for the Markdown twins and the agent surfaces, which are cheap to serve and meant to be read in bulk.

assistant.description: Assistant questions, which cost a model call each.

auth.description: Sign-in attempts, which is the limit that matters for guessing passwords.

builds.description: What one project's builds may use on the server.

concurrencyPerProject.description: How many builds of one project run at once. Above one, two builds of the same project compete for the same cache.

queue.description: How many builds may wait before one is refused.

cpu.description: CPU cores one build may use.

leaseSeconds.description: How long a worker holds a job before another may take it, which is what stops a crashed worker from stranding work.

offline.description: Run with no outbound network at all: no model calls, no spec fetches, no link checking.

server.description: Server-mode settings that are not secrets; only meaningful to `liyasa serve`.

csp.description: Additions to the Content Security Policy the build emits. The policy is generated; these keys widen it where a site needs something the default refuses.

extraScriptSrc.description: Extra sources scripts may load from.

extraImgSrc.description: Extra sources images may load from.

extraFrameSrc.description: Extra sources that may be framed in a page.

reportUri.description: Where the browser posts a report when the policy blocks something.

imgHostsAllow.description: Remote image hosts a page may load from, added to `img-src`. A host listed here also stops the build warning about the remote image it serves.

items.description: Remote image hosts added to `img-src` without W0719.

frameAncestors.description: Hosts that may embed this site's pages in a frame. Empty, none may.

items.description: Hosts allowed to embed frame-mode pages.

styleAttribute.description: What happens to a `style` attribute in content: `allowlist` keeps the declarations that cannot load or leak anything, `off` removes the attribute.

uploads.description: What a reader or an editor may upload.

allowTypes.description: Media types accepted. Anything else is refused at upload rather than served later.

svg.description: `sanitize` strips the script and external references out of an uploaded SVG; `attachment` serves it as a download so no browser executes it.

hstsPreload.description: Add `preload` to `Strict-Transport-Security` (RX-112). Off by default: preload is a one-way submission to browser lists.

oneOf.description: On or off, using the generated defaults.
The fields to publish, such as `Contact` and `Expires`.

security.description: Content Security Policy, frame ancestors, and upload rules (§30.2).

allowPrivate.description: Hosts or CIDRs that may be reached even though they are private addresses. Empty, a fetch to a private address is refused, which is what stops a config from reaching into the network the build runs on.

allowInsecureHosts.description: Hosts that may be reached over plain HTTP.

allowHosts.description: Hosts each kind of fetch may reach, listed separately so widening one does not widen the others.

specRefs.description: Hosts an OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document may pull a reference from.

factSources.description: Hosts a fact may read its value from.

agentFetch.description: Hosts the agent may fetch while it works.

embeds.description: Hosts a page may embed content from.

denyHosts.description: Hosts nothing may reach, whatever the allow lists say.

network.description: Outbound network allow lists, consumed by `liyasa-net` (§30.2.3).

display.description: How an endpoint's request appears: `interactive` lets a reader send it, `simple` shows it without sending, `none` shows the documentation alone.

proxy.description: Sending a playground request through the site's server rather than from the reader's browser, which is how a request reaches an API that does not allow cross-origin calls.

allow.description: Hosts the proxy may forward to. Nothing else is forwarded, so the proxy cannot be used to reach anything else.

languages.description: Code samples to generate for each request, in the order they are shown; the first is the one a reader sees.

requiredOnly.description: Show only the required parameters until a reader asks for the rest.

baseUrl.description: The base URL a manual API page's requests are sent to.

auth.description: How a manual API page's requests are authenticated.

method.description: The scheme: a bearer token, HTTP basic, an API key, or nothing.

name.description: The header, query parameter, or cookie the API key is sent as.

in.description: Where the API key is sent: in a header, in the query string, or in a cookie.

changelog.description: Publish the changelog as RSS, Atom, and JSON feeds.

updates.description: Publish a feed of every page that changed, not only the changelog.

fallback.description: What a reader sees when a page has no translation in their locale: the default locale's text under a notice, or nothing at all.

routeVisitors.description: Send a reader to the locale their browser asks for. Off, a reader stays where they navigated.

url.description: Where the author's name links to.

avatar.description: Path or URL of the author's avatar.

authors.description: Author handles resolved from front matter `authors`.

files.description: Skill files published for an agent to read.

groups.description: Access groups a skill file is limited to.

integration.description: A third-party integration: CFG-81's `{ id, consent }`. Enabled when present and not `false` or `null`.

oneOf.description: The integration's settings.

id.description: The account, site, or measurement id the third-party script is loaded with.

consent.description: `required` holds the script until the reader consents; `none` loads it immediately, which suits an integration that sets no cookie and follows nobody.

oneOf.description: `true` enables the integration with its defaults; `false` disables it.
`null` disables the integration, which is how an environment overlay switches one off.

navigationNode.description: One node of the navigation tree (§8.4). Every object form is discriminated by its own key.

oneOf.description: A page by path or route.
A collapsible group of pages in the sidebar.

tag.description: Short badge beside the label, such as `new` or `beta`.

root.description: A page the group's own label links to, rather than the label being inert.

pages.description: The group's entries. A glob such as `getting-started/*` expands to the pages under it, ordered by `order` front matter and then by title.

groups.description: Access groups that may see this subtree. A reader in none of them is served as if it did not exist.

regions.description: Regions this subtree belongs to; a reader outside them does not see it.

hidden.description: Keep the subtree routable but out of the sidebar.

oneOf.description: Every page under a directory, as a group generated from the files.

directory.description: The directory to generate from. Labels and order come from each page's front matter, and `index.md` becomes the group's root page.

groups.description: Access groups that may see this subtree.

hidden.description: Keep the subtree routable but out of the sidebar.

oneOf.description: A top-level tab, with a sidebar of its own.

groups.description: Access groups that may see this tab.

hidden.description: Keep the tab routable but out of the navbar.

oneOf.description: A dropdown menu in the navbar, holding tabs, groups, or links.

menu.description: The menu's label in the navbar.

items.description: What the menu holds: tabs, groups, or links.

oneOf.description: A global anchor, shown above the sidebar on every tab.

color.description: Accent colour for this anchor alone, as any CSS colour.

oneOf.description: A dropdown inside the sidebar, which is how a site switches between products.
A subtree that exists only for one value of a content dimension.

product.description: The dimension value this subtree belongs to; it must be one `dimensions` declares.

oneOf.description: A subtree that exists only in one version.

version.description: The version this subtree belongs to; it must be one `versions` declares.

oneOf.description: A subtree that exists only in one locale.

language.description: The locale this subtree belongs to; it must be one `locales` declares.

oneOf.description: Endpoint pages generated from an OpenAPI document.

openapi.description: The spec to generate from, by the `id` it was given under `openapi`.

oneOf.description: Every operation in the document.
Only these operations, written as `GET /users` or as operation ids.

operations.description: Which operations to generate pages for.

groupBy.description: Whether generated pages are grouped by their tag or by their path.

order.description: The order the groups appear in; anything not named follows in the document's own order.

labels.description: Display names for groups, keyed by the tag or path they replace.

oneOf.description: Channel and message pages generated from an AsyncAPI document.

asyncapi.description: The spec to generate from, by the `id` it was given under `asyncapi`.

oneOf.description: Type and operation pages generated from a GraphQL schema.

graphql.description: The schema to generate from, by the `id` it was given under `graphql`.

oneOf.description: SDK reference pages generated from a documentation export.

sdk.description: The language the reference is for, such as `typescript`.

source.description: The export to generate from, such as a `typedoc.json`.

oneOf.description: A link to somewhere outside the site, placed anywhere in the tree.
A heading in the sidebar that separates what follows; it collapses nothing and links nowhere.
